subject.title: fix(agents): skip error classification for clean non-zero exits

question: How should exec calls explicitly distinguish an expected non-zero outcome from an unexpected command failure for channel-warning purposes?
rationale: The current `completed` status only proves that the process terminated; choosing whether to add accepted exit codes, require shell normalization, or suppress every normally exited failure changes the public exec-result and notification contract.

options.title: Add an explicit expected-exit signal
options.body: Carry accepted exit codes or a typed expected-nonzero outcome through the exec result while retaining warnings for all other non-zero exits.

options.title: Keep the existing warning contract
options.body: Close or revise this PR and require commands expecting non-zero outcomes to normalize them explicitly, such as through shell control flow.

options.title: Suppress every completed non-zero exit
options.body: Approve the proposed broad suppression and accept that genuine normally terminated command failures may become silent in channels.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit expected-exit signal
recommendation.body: Carry accepted exit codes or a typed expected-nonzero outcome through the exec result while retaining warnings for all other non-zero exits.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is recent work on the same user-visible tool-warning policy and its tests.
